emailSubject: FMB News | La Mesa Dam Breaches Critical Water Level Amid Habagat Rains | August 9, 2026 | 12:00 PM PHT
headline: La Mesa Dam Rises Above Critical Level Amid Habagat Rains
deck: La Mesa Dam reached 79.77 meters on Sunday morning, above its 79.50-meter critical level but still below the 80.15-meter overflow level.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: La Mesa Dam's water level reached 79.77 meters at 10:20 a.m. on August 9, according to the state weather bureau's figures reported by GMA News. That placed the reservoir 27 centimeters above its 79.50-meter critical level and 38 centimeters below its 80.15-meter overflow level.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: La Mesa has an ungated spillway, so excess water flows out once the reservoir reaches its overflow level. Residents in low-lying communities along the Tullahan River were advised to monitor official warnings and prepare for possible flooding.

Persistent southwest monsoon rains continued to affect Luzon. The Office of Civil Defense said roughly 110,000 families had been affected by recent storms and the habagat, while about 7,300 people were staying in 86 evacuation centers as of August 8.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: La Mesa Dam supplies part of Metro Manila's water system and drains into the Tullahan River. Its ungated spillway makes current reservoir and downstream river monitoring especially important during prolonged rain.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: The bulletin supplied higher national totals for affected and displaced residents, but those figures could not be reconciled with the accessible official record at publication time. FMB News has therefore not presented them as confirmed. Water levels and evacuation counts can also change during continuing rainfall.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: La Mesa is a key water source for Metro Manila. Because the spillway is ungated, communities downstream need timely, location-specific warnings when the reservoir approaches the overflow mark.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: PAGASA and local disaster offices will continue monitoring rainfall, reservoir levels and river conditions. Residents should rely on current local government and PAGASA advisories rather than the measurements in this report alone.
